project: This background layer has some fancy parallax behaviors set to it, to give the illusion of distance.
For this example, the objects layer gets populated in the main loop of the 'TMX Parser' eventsheet. You can manually put objects in this layer if you so desire, but for now it's automated!

The collision layer is super important - the TMX Parser event will only parse a TMX/tilemap that is in this layer. Also, this is the only layer that applies the 'solid' behavior to a tilemap. You can put objects in this layer if you want, but if you put a tilemap in a different layer, you will need to make sure there is an event that sets is as a solid.
Although these scroll zones can vary in size, they cannot be smaller than one full grid square (by default, 320x176)

Hey you! See these red boxes in the camera layer? They're super important - they represent a 'scroll zone', and the camera will only scroll as long as the player is inside a scroll zone object. Each rectangle represents a game screen, and each rectangle needs to be  a complete screen in order for the game to scroll smoothly. See 1-2 for a vertical zone example.
How to play: Press A key to run, S key to jump, arrows to move.
Как играть: клавиша A для бега, клавиша S для прыжка, стрелки для перемещения.

Hey you! So you'll notice there's a couple of things going on in this level - tube warping, and multiple songs in scroll zones! Scroll zone songs must be changed manually, using the "music" attribute. You can put whatever you want in there, and as long as the player is in the scroll zone, it'll play the appropriate music.

Warping is a little tricky. Obviously they have to be added manually, after the level is created. Make sure half of the warper is overlapping the tilemap in any of the 4 directions. You also have to 1. manually set the ID of the current warper, and 2. set the ID of the warper you want to warp to. I suggest using a pen and paper to keep track!
